 Community News Crews Wrap Central Library’s Great Hall Roof Ahead of Rainy Season
 The 1927 landmark has been closed since May 2021, with completion targeted for summer 2028
 Published on Friday, October 30, 2026 | 5:24 am 
 Rebar capping in the basement of Central Library. [photo credit; City of Pasadena] Crews retrofitting Pasadena’s Central Library have fully covered the roof over the Great Hall with plastic sheeting to protect the cork floor and historic interior beneath it as the rainy season approaches, according to the City of Pasadena.
 The work is part of the Phase 2 construction phase of a project whose contract with PCL Construction Services, Inc. the City Council raised on March 2 to a not-to-exceed total of $186,186,155. The 135,000-square-foot building at 285 E. Walnut St. has been closed since May 3, 2021, after a structural assessment found it was largely unreinforced masonry and vulnerable to collapse in an earthquake.
 Shotcrete installation continues on schedule, rebar is being fitted with safety caps over sharp exposed ends, and shoring permits for the Circulation Hall have been approved, with preparation work to begin soon to support the final demolition activities, Tim McDonald, director of libraries and information services, reported. A city project update dated Oct. 22 said basement footing and slab pours were expected to be finished by the end of the month, except in the Circulation Hall, and that removal of historic wood ceiling panels in the Reading Room was complete.
 Pasadena voters approved Measure PL, a $195 million general obligation bond, in November 2024 with 72.42 percent of the vote, above the two-thirds threshold it required, according to the City Clerk’s certified canvass. The bond levies $28.90 per $100,000 of assessed valuation. Debra Gerod, a partner at design firm Gruen Associates, told LAist in 2024 that the $195 million covers total project costs, including furniture and project management.
 An Aug. 24 staff report to the City Council put the base construction contract at $164,945,066 and, with $714,543 in approved change orders, the current construction contract value at $165,659,609. The city had drawn about $11.74 million in bond proceeds through June 30, and construction was proceeding in accordance with the baseline schedule, the report said.
 The Mediterranean Revival-style library, designed by Myron Hunt and H.C. Chambers and dedicated Feb. 12, 1927, was the first building completed under Pasadena’s Civic Center Plan and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Pasadena adopted an ordinance in 1993 requiring unreinforced masonry buildings to be retrofitted, vacated or demolished, and no records showed why the library had not been identified as one, CBS Los Angeles reported in 2021. “This is devastating news for us all,” then-City Manager Steve Mermell said when the building closed, according to CBS.
 Since the closure, books have been moved to the city’s branch libraries or stored in a warehouse, and patrons can order titles shipped to a branch but cannot browse the collection, LAist reported in 2024. The auditorium had hosted more than 500 programs in the year before the closure, McDonald told LAist. “We’re not able to connect and bring people together in our branches,” he said.
 Completion is targeted for summer 2028, according to the city, and the building’s 100th anniversary falls on Feb. 12, 2027. Project information is posted at   https://www.cityofpasadena. net/library/central-library- earthquake-retrofit/  and construction updates at   https://www.cityofpasadena. net/library/central-library- updates/ .
